summary:
Product NOT READY. Independently drove unchanged packaged desktop 1.3.0 at Aether a995c38369c4a731dadc07d5227fece4f40bff24 and Archon 8feab04942fc476904262519da243554bdf9d9c5; verified all four build artifact hashes. Real Haiku and Luna lessons ran sequentially with allow_api=false, answered eight/four diagnostic questions including deliberate errors, reached teaching and extracted graph data. First visible content: Haiku 19.758 s; Luna 24.141 s, complete chunks rather than measured streamed tokens.
Scenario table: J1 First launch PASS; J2 Settings/providers/models FAIL; J3 Haiku lesson FAIL; J4 Luna lesson FAIL; J5 Persistence FAIL; J6 Billing truth FAIL; J7 Basic regression/all navigation PASS.
Seven product findings: text model fields without readiness choices; missing answer grades; prober transcript replacement and historical question loss after reopening; stale open graph after extraction; Luna extraction yielded three nodes but no links; no per-lesson subscription attribution (generic dollar estimates do not prove API charges); no incremental streaming observed. Saved sessions/plans/open questions/graph/settings/usage survived restart exactly, and Luna continued to 1/2 plan steps done. Normal Haiku chat and all top-level screens worked. No journey renderer errors, failed requests, unhandled exceptions or daemon errors/panics. Retained original preload TypeError and setup plain-launch control supporting the CDP-timing exception.
Results: .archon/reports/e2e/results.json; detailed findings.json and REPORT.txt; 47 steps, 86 screenshots, console/daemon logs and timing captures. Published directory e2e-validation-results for this item. Environment had no blocking problems; documented CDP/headless-Sway deviations and locator mistakes. Product source and branch unchanged. All 28 recorded process identities stopped, no build slot held; shutdown preceded the operator's run-lean amendment and no further processes will start. Only the report stage remains.
VERDICT: PASS

findings.detail: J3 Haiku, J4 Luna and J5 Persistence. Product at fault; environment was operational. Steps: 1. Finish diagnostic answers. 2. Enter plan/teaching. 3. Quit desktop and both daemons. 4. Restart and reopen both lessons. Expected: Full learner/teacher transcript, questions, answers and results remain available across phase changes and restart. Actual: Handoff removes prior prober teacher messages and inserts internal assessment JSON as You. Restart/reopen removes all eight Haiku and four Luna diagnostic question cards. Relevant captured output: Conversation begins "You: Learning goal: How binary search works The Prober's assessment: { ... }"; only the current Choose question remains. Before: eight diagnostic article cards plus the teaching card. Suspected area: Learn session transcript hydration / prober-to-teacher handoff. Evidence: .archon/reports/e2e/assets/j5-haiku-persisted.txt:68.
findings.title: J3/J4/J5: Prober transcript replaced and historical questions disappear on reopening

findings.detail: J3 Haiku graph extraction. Product at fault; environment was operational. Steps: 1. In Haiku teaching click Add to knowledge graph. 2. Open Knowledge before extraction completes. 3. Observe completion through public noesis_graph and wait another 15 seconds. Expected: Open graph refreshes to show completed nodes and links, as queued status promises. Actual: Wire had five nodes and one chain at 15:15:34 UTC, but open UI stayed empty. A later normal navigation visit showed the stored graph without another extraction. Command used for the failing observation: node .archon/reports/e2e/drive.mjs j3-graph-complete < .archon/reports/e2e/assets/j3-graph-complete.action.js. Relevant captured output: locator.waitFor: Timeout 15000ms exceeded; region "The graph is empty" remained visible. noesis_graph returned nodes[5], chains[1]. Suspected area: Knowledge view refresh / extraction completion event handling. Evidence: .archon/reports/e2e/assets/j3-graph-complete.txt:74.
findings.title: J3: Open graph stays empty after successful extraction

findings.detail: J4 Luna graph extraction. Product at fault; environment was operational. Steps: 1. Reach Luna teaching after four diagnostic answers. 2. Click Add to knowledge graph. 3. Inspect completed graph filtered to this session. Expected: Luna lesson graph contains nodes and links, as required by the journey. Actual: Three nodes and zero chains. Combined UI has links only from the earlier Haiku session. Cause is unproven: this is a failed link-coverage acceptance check for this lesson, not proof that all Luna extraction is broken. findings.title: J4: Luna extraction produced nodes but no links

findings.detail: J6 Billing truth. Product at fault; environment was operational. Steps: 1. Run both subscription lessons with Allow API-billed models off. 2. Inspect lesson pages and Learn settings spend. Expected: Per-lesson usage explicitly identified as subscription, distinct from API dollar charges. Actual: No lesson-specific subscription usage label. Relevant captured output: heading "Spent today"; $0.02 of $5.00; $0.01 of $1.00; "Subscription use counts at its estimated price." Suspected area: Learn usage/billing presentation. Evidence: .archon/reports/e2e/assets/j6-subscription-display.txt:90.
findings.title: J6: Lessons lack explicit subscription usage attribution

findings.detail: J3 Haiku and J4 Luna streaming. Product at fault; environment was operational. Steps: 1. Observe main DOM mutations immediately before Start session. 2. Start each engine lesson. 3. Compare successive visible text updates. Expected: Lesson text streams incrementally while the engine generates it. Actual: Haiku introduction/question first appeared together at 19.758 s; Luna first question appeared complete at 24.141 s. No incremental first-token stream was observed. Timings are first visible content, not true streamed-token latency. Command used for the failing observation: node .archon/reports/e2e/drive.mjs j4-observe </dev/null (MutationObserver installed by j4-start). Relevant captured output: DOM observations: 0.928 s user learning goal only; 24.141 s complete question/options. Haiku: 10.649 s user goal; 19.758 s complete introduction/question. Suspected area: Subscription engine delta delivery / Learn streaming presentation. Evidence: .archon/reports/e2e/assets/j4-observe.timing.json:22.
findings.title: J3/J4: Content appears in complete chunks rather than incremental streaming

findings.detail: Product fault. Start a long normal chat, confirm the desktop restart action while it runs, and inspect the resumed response. Expected: The resumed agent continues the requested work or accurately explains a system restart. Actual: After Connect Archon tools restarted the live turn, the agent says the interrupt came from you and asks whether to resume. The process resumed, but the requested tutorial did not continue without a reply. UI transcript: The 3,000-word decimal-versus-binary tutorial was interrupted before I wrote any of it, and the interrupt came from you. I have not restarted it... Do you want me to write it now? Evidence: ["assets/polish-restart-misattribution.png"].
findings.title: J12 P4: Normal chat misattributes desktop restart to a deliberate user interruption

summary:
NOT READY. Completed all 15 packaged-app journeys against Aether 06454742, Archon 1.5.0 b5f38dba and 1.4.12 611aaa8b. Results are trustworthy: 12 pass, 3 fail, none environment-blocked.

Scenario table: J1 First launch PASS; J2 Settings/models PASS; J3 Haiku Learn FAIL; J4 Luna Learn PASS; J5 Learn from work PASS; J6 Budget stall PASS; J7 Persistence PASS; J8 Billing PASS; J9 Archon1.5 desktop PASS; J10 Archon1.4.12 PASS; J11 Native desktop PASS with documented substitutions; J12 Live-agent restarts PASS with diagnostic observation; J13 Memory PASS; J14 Regression sweep FAIL; J15 Size/speed FAIL (palette recovery).

Haiku had an ambiguous choice, repeated completed material with mismatched feedback, and stalled before a third distinct taught step. An interrupted tool became Failed after reload. Palette Retry failed twice after the injected chunk fault was cleared. Luna completed four distinct graded steps. Both teaching/practice SIGTERM recovery and F6 concurrent operations passed; all38 enforced perf rows and21 tests passed. Captured216 native layout screenshots, measured1024px chat transcript393.98px high, and verified3440 completion alignment. Five primary defects, nine polish items and two lifecycle observations are documented.

findings.detail: Product fault. Expected: The load error is visible, Close/Escape dismiss it, and Retry loads the now-available chunk. Actual: Close and Escape work. Retry twice returns the same dynamic-import error. A full page reload restores the palette. Command: page.route("**/assets/entity-palette-*.js", route => route.abort("failed")); open Jump to; page.unroute(...); click Try again. Output: The palette failed; Failed to fetch dynamically imported module: app://aether/assets/entity-palette-BM8xmEpF.js. Repeated once with the same result. Initial fault was intentional; failed recovery after clearing it is product behavior. Suspected palette/lazy-import retry cache; implementation not inspected.
